_comment: Pinned SG13CMOS5L PDK revision this sim/sg13cmos5l-*/ evidence records were generated against. A NEW file, not a restructuring of sim/pdk.json (issue #65's Builder's-call decision): sim/pdk.json's own schema (release_tag + tarball_sha256) assumes a tagged tarball release, which is how IHP-Open-PDK/SG13G2 ships (see sim/pdk.json), but SG13CMOS5L (as of this pin) ships only as a live 'main'-branch git checkout with no tags/releases at all -- forcing that schema onto a git-commit pin would either lie (fabricate a fake tarball_sha256) or require reshaping the schema for both PDKs at once, more churn than this phase's scope needs. A restructured, PDK-keyed sim/pdk.json remains an option for a future phase if a third PDK variant lands and the two schemas converge; not done here to keep this phase's footprint to 'add a CMOS5L fact sheet', matching design/sg13cmos5l/README.md's own choice to add a new subdirectory rather than restructure design/'s existing SG13G2 layout. Every record under sim/sg13cmos5l-*/records/*.md must trace to this file (or a later commit that bumps it) -- see sim/README.md 'PDK pin, per variant' section.
fetch_method: git clone https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/ihp-sg13cmos5l.git -- no tagged release exists yet (repo README: 'meant to be used only as a temporary storage during the development of the build/compile migration script'); this repo pins a commit on the 'main' branch, not a checksummed tarball. Re-verify commit reachability (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <pinned_commit> main`) rather than assuming immutability the way a tagged tarball would guarantee.
pdk_root_layout: PDK_ROOT/ihp-sg13cmos5l (open_pdks-shaped install, klt pdk find/list convention) -- same PDK_ROOT sim/pdk.json's ihp-sg13g2 install already resolves from, see 'sibling_checkout_requirement' below for why both must coexist under one PDK_ROOT.
relationship_to_ihp_sg13g2: SG13CMOS5L is IHP's reduced-metal-stack CMOS-only sibling process to SG13G2, not an unrelated third PDK -- confirmed directly from the installed checkout (see spec/porting-plan-sg13cmos5l.md section 1). Front-end devices this repo's schematics use (sg13_hv_pmos/nmos, pnpMPA, rppd/rhigh) are the SAME models as SG13G2's: sg13cmos5l_pr's .sym files and this PDK's own libs.tech/ngspice/models/*.lib corner files for those devices (cornerMOShv.lib, cornerRES.lib, sg13g2_moshv_mod.lib, etc. -- note the literal sg13g2_*.lib filenames even under the ihp-sg13cmos5l tree) are relative SYMLINKS into a sibling ihp-sg13g2 checkout, not independent copies.

sibling_checkout_requirement._comment: A real, upstream-worthy PDK-tooling gap, filed per CLAUDE.md's friction protocol at 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#1406 (design/sg13cmos5l/README.md 'Tooling/PDK friction encountered' has the full account from issue #64/#68's own discovery of the xschem-symbol half of this same gap). This sim/ phase (#65) hit the SAME dangling-symlink pattern independently for the ngspice corner-lib files (cornerMOShv.lib, cornerRES.lib, sg13g2_moshv_mod.lib, etc. under libs.tech/ngspice/models/), not just the xschem symbols #1406 already covers -- same root cause (an ihp-sg13cmos5l-only install has no sibling ihp-sg13g2/ to resolve the relative symlink target against), different file class. Not re-filed as a second issue: #1406's own description already generalizes to 'this PDK's install-shape assumption is a combined checkout', which covers both file classes.
sibling_checkout_requirement.requirement: PDK_ROOT must contain BOTH ihp-sg13g2/ and ihp-sg13cmos5l/ side by side (this PDK's own README.md documents this as the intended install shape: 'git clone --branch dev --recurse-submodules https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK.git; cd IHP-Open-PDK; git clone https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/ihp-sg13cmos5l.git'). An ihp-sg13cmos5l-only install leaves every shared-device symlink dangling and every sim/sg13cmos5l-*/ testbench in this tree unrunnable.
sibling_checkout_requirement.how_this_repo_resolved_it_in_this_enviro: Fetched IHP-Open-PDK v0.3.0's tarball (the same release + sha256 sim/pdk.json already pins for the SG13G2-only tree) and extracted only its ihp-sg13g2/ subtree as a sibling of the existing ihp-sg13cmos5l/ checkout under the shared PDK_ROOT -- no design/xschemrc or sim/env.sh change needed or made, since both already resolve PDK_ROOT/PDK generically from the environment. This is an environment-setup step, not a repo change; a fresh environment must repeat it (or install the combined checkout this PDK's own README documents) before any sim/sg13cmos5l-*/ testbench can run.

osdi_toolchain._comment: Unlike SG13G2 v0.3.0 (which ships Verilog-A SOURCES only and needs sim/tools/build-osdi.sh's full compile step -- see sim/pdk.json), this ihp-sg13cmos5l checkout at the pinned commit above ships PREBUILT .osdi binaries already, confirmed by direct listing of libs.tech/ngspice/osdi/. spec/porting-plan-sg13cmos5l.md section 1 flagged this as unconfirmed-stable across releases ('whether this holds for whatever release phase 2 (#65) actually pins is unconfirmed'); THIS PIN CONFIRMS IT HOLDS at commit 607e18d4.
osdi_toolchain.install_dir: PDK_ROOT/ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.tech/ngspice/osdi (PDK-install territory, not tracked in this repo, same convention as sim/pdk.json's SG13G2 entry)
osdi_toolchain.build_script_still_works_generically: sim/tools/build-osdi.sh --check (which sim/lib/pvt_preflight.sh calls unconditionally, regardless of $PDK) resolves PDK_ROOT/$PDK generically via sim/env.sh, so it passes for PDK=ihp-sg13cmos5l with zero code changes -- verified directly: it finds all four REQUIRED_OSDI files already present and loads them in a real ngspice model-instantiation check. No sim/tools/build-osdi.sh edits were made or needed for this phase; the script was never modified to be 'CMOS5L-aware', it simply already generalizes.

bipolar_device_note._comment: SG13CMOS5L has no npn13G2-equivalent HBT -- only pnpMPA, a low-gain (bf ~= 1.10 nominal, corner-swept via cornerPNP.lib below) parasitic-style PNP. See spec/decision-records/0004-cmos5l-bipolar-device-selection.md (DR-0004).
bipolar_device_note.process_corner_file: libs.tech/ngspice/models/cornerPNP.lib (a REAL file in this checkout, not a symlink -- confirmed by direct listing)
bipolar_device_note.no_skewed_pnp_sections: Unlike cornerMOShv.lib (which has mos_sf/mos_fs skew corners), cornerPNP.lib has no sf/fs-equivalent skew section -- same shape as SG13G2's own cornerHBT.lib (hbt_typ/hbt_bcs/hbt_wcs only). This repo's sim/lib/pvt_preflight.sh HBT_SECTION_OF map already falls the sf/fs grid points back to the typ section for exactly this reason; this phase's own sg13cmos5l-*/run_pvt_sweep.sh scripts define an equivalent PNP_SECTION_OF map with the identical sf/fs->typ fallback, kept local to those scripts rather than added to the shared pvt_preflight.sh (SG13G2's testbenches never reference a PNP section at all, so adding it to shared code would be dead weight there).

supply_rails._comment: Per spec/porting-plan-sg13cmos5l.md's own clarification: this repo's bandgap-only block uses ONLY the 3.3V HV-flavor analog rail (sg13_hv_nmos/pmos, identical device+rating to SG13G2's own DR-0002 choice) -- the parent epic's '1.2V digital / 3.3V analog' framing names SG13CMOS5L's LV-flavor DIGITAL rail, which this analog-only block never instantiates a device against. issue #65's PVT sweep therefore uses the SAME {2.97, 3.30, 3.63} V grid (+-10% of 3.3V) as every existing SG13G2 sim/ testbench, not a second 1.2V rail sweep -- there is no 1.2V-rated device anywhere in design/sg13cmos5l/*.sch to sweep.
